findings.title: Fatal error originates in a theme

evidence.excerpt: [11-Sep-2026 09:02:51 UTC] PHP Fatal error:  Uncaught TypeError: storefront_post_meta(): Argument #1 ($post) must be of type WP_Post, null given in /var/www/html/wp-content/themes/storefront/inc/storefront-template-functions.php:288

findings.cause:
The reported fatal error was raised from a file inside wp-content/themes, so the active theme is the immediate source of the failure. Ownership is taken from the parsed error signature; this rule does not attribute ownership itself.

Error class: TypeError
Message: storefront_post_meta(): Argument #1 ($post) must be of type WP_Post, null given
File: /var/www/html/wp-content/themes/storefront/inc/storefront-template-functions.php
Line: 288
Ownership confidence: directory name not in the catalog, so the owner is identified by path only
findings.fix: Switch temporarily to a default theme such as Storefront or Twenty Twenty-Four. If the error stops, the fault is in the theme and should go to its author, or to whoever maintains the child theme if the file lives there.
findings.reproducibilityImpact: Theme-owned failures reproduce only if the exact theme and version are obtainable. A custom or child theme is usually not available, which limits reproduction.
